# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 66

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 66:1 "assigned to me" vs. "been assigned to me"

- **EMET:** "why has this angel of punishment been assigned to me"
- **LOGOS:** "why has this angel of punishment been assigned to me"
- **PNEUMA:** "why have I been assigned to this angel of punishment"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree; PNEUMA reverses the passive subject.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "why has this angel of punishment been assigned to me" (EMET/LOGOS). The original question is about the angel's assignment to Hermas, not Hermas's assignment to the angel — keeping the angel as grammatical subject.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 66:1 "as a chastisement" vs. "for chastisement"

- **EMET:** "delivered to this angel as a chastisement"
- **LOGOS:** "delivered to this angel for chastisement"
- **PNEUMA:** "You were delivered to this angel for discipline"
- **Greek:** *eis tou basanisthaī* — for the purpose of being afflicted/punished
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "delivered to this angel for chastisement" (LOGOS). The purpose clause is clearer with "for" than "as."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 66:1 "humble you" vs. "bring you low"

- **EMET:** "afflict you and make you humble"
- **LOGOS:** "afflict you and humble you"
- **PNEUMA:** "humble you and bring you low"
- **Greek:** *basanisē kai tapeinōsē* — afflict/torment and humble
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "afflict you and humble you" (LOGOS). Two verbs; the repetition in PNEUMA ("humble you and bring you low") loses one distinct term.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 66:2 "not all that great" vs. "not so great"

- **EMET:** "not all that great, so that you should be delivered"
- **LOGOS:** "not so great that you should be delivered to this angel permanently"
- **PNEUMA:** "not so extreme that you had to be permanently assigned"
- **Note:** Minor variation.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not so great that you had to be delivered to this angel permanently" (LOGOS/PNEUMA blend). LOGOS's "permanently" is an implicit extrapolation but contextually appropriate; PNEUMA's "extreme" over-translates.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 66:2 "great and terrible iniquities" — all agree

- **EMET:** "great and terrible iniquities against the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "great and terrible iniquities against the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "great and terrible sins against the Lord"
- **Note:** Only PNEUMA varies ("sins" vs. "iniquities").
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "great and terrible iniquities against the Lord." *Anomiai* = lawlessnesses/iniquities; "iniquities" is more formal.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 66:3 "I did not sin against the Lord" — all agree

- **EMET:** "I did not sin against the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "I have not sinned against the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "I didn't sin against the Lord"
- **Note:** Minor tense variation.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I have not sinned against the Lord." The perfect tense ("have not sinned") represents the ongoing claim of innocence more precisely.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 66:3 "allowed it to become completely corrupt" vs. "allowed it to fall into complete corruption"

- **EMET:** "allowed it to become completely corrupt"
- **LOGOS:** "allowed it to fall into complete corruption"
- **PNEUMA:** "allowed it to become completely corrupt"
- **Greek:** *eiasas autēn diaphthareīnai* — allowed it to be thoroughly corrupted
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "allowed it to fall into complete corruption" (LOGOS). "Fall into corruption" suggests the progressive degradation more graphically than the static "become corrupt."

---

## Disagreement 8 — 66:4 "cannot be saved quickly" — all agree

- **EMET:** "they cannot be saved quickly"
- **LOGOS:** "they cannot be saved quickly"
- **PNEUMA:** "they can't be saved quickly"
- **Note:** All agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they cannot be saved quickly." The time qualifier is important — not that salvation is impossible, but that it requires the full term.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 66:4 "be subdued" vs. "be brought low" vs. "be brought low"

- **EMET:** "must go through his torments and be subdued"
- **LOGOS:** "must complete his torments and be brought low"
- **PNEUMA:** "has to go through the full extent of their torments, be brought low"
- **Greek:** *tapeinōthēi* — to be humbled/brought low/subdued
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "must complete his torments and be brought low" (LOGOS). "Be brought low" preserves the humility root (*tapeinoo*) which is thematically significant throughout the Shepherd.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 66.*
